pattern: 97% (168 of 173) of Cognitive Services/AI accounts have publicNetworkAccess Enabled and only 25 of 173 (14%) have disableLocalAuth True
implication: For a security-prioritized isolated dev AI resource, deviate from the tenant default: set publicNetworkAccess to Disabled (or restrict via networkAcls) and disableLocalAuth to True, relying on Microsoft Entra ID/OIDC-based auth rather than API keys.

pattern: 100% (173 of 173) of Cognitive Services accounts use SKU S0, and identity is systemAssigned for 63 of 173 (36%), with the remainder none/unassigned
implication: Provision the new AI account with SKU S0 and a system-assigned managed identity to align with tenant conventions and support keyless authentication.

pattern: 184 user-assigned managed identities exist tenant-wide, and multiple resource types predominantly use userAssigned identity
implication: Create dedicated user-assigned managed identities scoped to the new resource group for GitHub Actions OIDC federation rather than reusing identities from other workloads.

pattern: Only 8 of 173 Cognitive Services accounts have private endpoint connections configured; the vast majority rely on public network access
implication: For the low-volume development scenario, public network access with Entra authorization avoids private networking cost and remains reachable from GitHub-hosted runners.

pattern: Tagging is inconsistent and sparse across resource types
implication: Apply environment, application, owner, repository, and managed-by tags on all new resources for ownership and cost tracking.

pattern: Resource and managed-identity naming frequently embeds the owner or project name
implication: Use gallery-scoped CAF-style names to avoid collisions and clarify ownership.

pattern: TLS-capable resources across the subscription overwhelmingly enforce TLS 1.2
implication: Enforce TLS 1.2 or later on every applicable new resource.
